sasha: Heads-up — I'm seeing a ~25% P95 latency bump on h100 pools after the driver upgrade this morning. Seems concentrated on long-context requests (seq_len >= 1024). Any ideas?

kai: yep saw the spike on the infra dash around 08:30 UTC. p99 up ~30%, overall throughput down ~18% on Dedicated. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~5% but only for the long-tail requests.

jena: Do we have the exact driver package/version and the deploy id? Could be cuBLAS/cuDNN ABI change that nudged kernel selection.

runtime-bot: deploy event: rollouts/deploy-2026-03-18-driver-544.23 completed -> h100-region-1 @ 08:12 UTC.

sasha: Repro steps I've been using (small script):
```bash
# stress long-context requests against dedicated pool
python perf_test.py --model rwd-large-v1 --seq 1536 --batch 1 --qps 30 --kv_cache true
```
Observed: latency step-up after first KV cache warmups; profiler shows more time in attention kernel and increased host-device syncs.

kai: I pulled a short perf sample with nvprof/ncu. Snapshot:
```
Time(%)  Name
24.7    attn_fused_v2_forward
12.1    softmax_kernel_optimized
8.3     memory_copy_async
6.9     cuBLAS_gemm_ex
```
This is different from yesterday where attn_v1_block dominated and was cheaper for our sequence shapes. Looks like the autotuner/heuristic is picking attn_fused_v2 now.

jena: If the kernel preference flipped due to updated driver kernels, autotuner DB entries might have been invalidated. Can you dump autotuner decisions?

kai: dumped autotuner DB (snippet):
```
# /var/lib/runtime/autotune/driver-544.23.db
{shape: [12, 1024], chosen: attn_fused_v2, score: 0.87}
{shape: [12, 1024], chosen: attn_v1_block, score: 0.85, timestamp: 1678901111}
```
We had previously favored attn_v1_block; new score calc bumped v2 slightly. But microbench harness shows v2 is slower for our end-to-end because of extra synchronization and worse KV cache locality.

sasha: Quick mitigation: we can force a kernel pin per-model or per-cluster until we sort root cause. Runtime supports RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL env or per-model config. Example config: 
```json
{"model_settings": {"rwd-large-v1": {"force_kernel": "attn_v1_block"}}}
```
I'll stage this on a canary 10% of traffic.

ops_oncall: Plan sounds good. Alternative is canary rollback of driver on a small pool. Reverting drivers has infra risk but may be cleaner if multiple kernels regressed. Proposed checklist:
- mark 10% of Dedicated nodes as canary
- apply config force_kernel on canary namespace
- run perf workload and observe p50/p95 and KV hit-rate for 30m
- if improves, roll to 50% then full; if not, revert to previous driver image.

jena: Also check batching heuristics: there was a new kernel that interacts poorly with continuous batching for seq>1024 and causes batcher to split into more micro-batches because of changed memory estimation. Look for increased batch_split_count in traces.

kai: I grepped traces: batch_split_count jumped ~40% for those flows. KV cache behavior: more cache misses (evictions) because attn_fused_v2 uses a different internal kv layout and increases per-layer workspace. That explains end-to-end regression even though microkernel bench on raw GEMM looks fine.

sasha: Posting a quick smoke plan:
1) apply force_kernel on canary nodes (10%) -> config: `force_kernel=attn_v1_block`
2) enable detailed autotuner logging on canary: `AUTOTUNE_VERBOSE=1`
3) run 30m perf test, collect p50/p95, throughput, KV hit-rate, batch_split_count
4) if p95 drops >=15% and throughput recovers, expand to 50%
5) else rollback driver on canary and open vendor ticket

jena: Agreed. Add a metric check for device-side memalloc failures or OOM nimbleness — attn_fused_v2 might request larger transient buffers and cause more CUDAAllocator churn.

ops_oncall: I'll provision the canary nodepool and tag nodes with `kernel-canary=true`. ETA 20m.

sasha: Meanwhile, I've prepared an emergency runtime flag to disable autotune entirely for affected shapes: `AUTOTUNE_DISABLE_SHAPES="12x1024,16x1536"`. If canary with force_kernel looks good, we can either keep the forced kernel or relax by disabling autotune for those shapes until upstream provides a fix.

kai: I'll collect a full perf capture and upload the ncu report to the thread in 15m.

runtime-bot: NOTE: When forcing kernels, be cautious — pinned kernels bypass future autotuner improvements. Add an expiry tag to the config change (24h) so it doesn't become permanent. :exclamation:

sasha: Good call. I'll set the canary config with `expires_in: 24h` and add a follow-up task for a proper root-cause RCA with vendor if needed.

jena: If we need to escalate, I'll loop in Nvidia support and add kernel snapshots + autotuner DB. For now let's run the canary.

ops_oncall: Canaries are up with `kernel-canary=true`. Applying force_kernel to canary now. Will post perf metrics in ~30m. :thumbsup:
